policy.statement: re-centre the position symmetrically at ±6% around the current spot price, on the 0.25% fee tier, keeping the same liquidity

case.why: A third-party TWT/WBNB position on PancakeSwap V3’s 0.25% tier, observed with nonzero liquidity at BSC block 131043602 on 1 November 2026. Its owner and NFT were selected from chain liquidity events before testing the agent. The former BNCB/WBNB primary (#7650656) and both old fallback positions had zero liquidity at block 131042505; their historical cases and results remain stored. Two newly observed positions with different owners are added ahead of the retained old fallback roster. Ownership and liquidity are read again at every fresh capture; if none survives, no passing result is invented. The policy, arithmetic assertions and tolerances are unchanged. The fixture measures V3 arithmetic, not the investment merits of its tokens.

checks.description: Reported current tick must equal the pool tick at the pinned block, exactly.
checks.rationale: The tick is a single integer read from slot0 at a fixed block. There is no ambiguity and therefore no tolerance.

checks.description: Every proposed tick must be an exact multiple of the pool’s tickSpacing.
checks.rationale: The pool contract reverts on a tick that is not a multiple of its spacing, so a plan that violates this is not merely suboptimal, it is unexecutable. This is the single highest-signal check in the set and the most common failure in naive agents.

checks.description: Proposed bounds must match the range implied by the policy SUPPLIED IN THE TEST CASE, within one tick spacing.
checks.rationale: There is no objectively correct V3 range in the abstract, so the case supplies the policy and we check compliance with it. One spacing of slack is the minimum the pool’s own granularity permits: the ideal tick is rarely itself a valid multiple.

checks.description: Proposed token amounts must satisfy the V3 liquidity formula within this tolerance.
checks.rationale: The formula is exact, but agents legitimately round for slippage and gas. 0.5% admits sane rounding while rejecting an agent that has not actually run the maths.

checks.description: The in-range boolean must match the chain.
checks.rationale: Derived from tickLower <= tick < tickUpper. One right answer.

checks.description: Distance to the nearest bound, in price terms.
checks.rationale: Derived arithmetic from the tick and the two bounds. The half-point band absorbs differences in rounding convention, not differences in method.

checks.description: A slippage bound must be stated, as a positive number.
checks.rationale: An execution plan with no slippage bound is unsafe to sign regardless of how good its range is. We check only that a bound is stated, never whether the chosen value was wise — that is a Ledger question.

policy.statement: build a 12-level grid for BNB/USDT between 600 and 850 using 2,000 USD of capital, with a stop at 580, and disclose the fee drag at 25 bps per trade

case.why: Bounds and a stop that are close enough together that a careless plan places levels below the stop, and a level count that makes fee drag material rather than a rounding error.

checks.description: Level spacing must match the declared spacing type (arithmetic or geometric).
checks.rationale: The agent declares which type it used; we then verify the levels actually follow it. Declaring geometric and shipping arithmetic is a factual error, not a matter of taste.

checks.description: Summed level allocations must not exceed the stated capital.
checks.rationale: Spending more than the capital supplied is unexecutable. The 0.1% band covers floating-point summation, nothing more.

checks.description: Every level must lie inside the bounds supplied by the test case.
checks.rationale: Compliance with a constraint the case supplied. One right answer.

checks.description: No level may sit below the stop supplied by the test case.
checks.rationale: A level below the stop would be filled and then immediately stopped out.

checks.description: The plan must disclose fee drag: n levels implies n round-trips of fees, stated as a number.
checks.rationale: A grid plan that omits fee drag overstates its own return, and the omission is invisible to the buyer. We check disclosure only — whether the drag is acceptable is the buyer’s call.

policy.statement: find the best net-of-cost route for 1,000 USD of USDT across the allowed protocols, only recommending a move that beats the current 0% by at least 50 bps, and excluding leveraged strategies

case.why: Idle stablecoins are the most common real position on BSC. The 50 bps threshold and the 1,000 USD size make the net-of-cost arithmetic decide the answer, which is exactly the thing agents get wrong by quoting gross APR.

checks.description: Every quoted APR must carry a source and a timestamp.
checks.rationale: An APR with no source and no timestamp cannot be checked by anyone, including the buyer. This is the yield-category equivalent of a provenance chip.

checks.description: Net APR at the stated size must reproduce ours within this tolerance.
checks.rationale: Both sides compute from the same on-chain rates at the same block, so the only legitimate divergence is gas and compounding convention. 15bps is generous for that and far tighter than the differences between real venues.

checks.description: The switching cost must be itemized, not given as a single opaque number.
checks.rationale: Gas, swap and exit costs behave differently with size. A lump sum hides which one dominates at the buyer’s size.

checks.description: A recommendation must clear the minimum-improvement threshold supplied by the test case, or the agent must decline to recommend.
checks.rationale: Compliance with a supplied constraint. Declining is a pass: an agent that correctly says "nothing beats your current position by enough" is behaving well.

checks.description: If the case excludes leverage, any leveraged strategy must be flagged as such.
checks.rationale: Presenting a looped position as a plain deposit misstates the risk the buyer is taking.

policy.statement: report the account’s current health factor and the exact USD of debt that must be repaid to restore a health factor of 2.5

case.why: A genuinely at-risk third-party Venus account carrying real debt across multiple collateral markets. Chosen precisely because it is not ours: it proves the reader works on arbitrary input, and AGENTS.md forbids manufacturing our own liquidation risk for a demo.

checks.description: Reported health factor must match ours to three decimal places.
checks.rationale: Both sides read the same Comptroller state at the same block, so this is pure arithmetic. 0.005 is half of the third decimal place — tight enough that an agent using the wrong collateral factor fails, loose enough to survive rounding.

checks.description: Per-market collateral factor must match the Comptroller.
checks.rationale: Read directly from markets(vToken). Getting this wrong is what makes an HF wrong.

checks.description: The repay amount must, when applied, restore the target health factor within this tolerance.
checks.rationale: Checked by APPLYING the agent’s number to the snapshot and recomputing, not by comparing to ours. An agent that reaches the target by a different but valid route passes.

checks.description: Per-asset liquidation price must match ours within this tolerance.
checks.rationale: A closed-form function of collateral, debt and collateral factors. One percent admits oracle rounding, not method error.

MCS-RYIELD-1.name: Realised Yield
MCS-RYIELD-1.reader: Venus vToken exchangeRateStored at two archived blocks, with their timestamps

policy.statement: measure what each Venus USDT supply market actually paid between the two supplied blocks, from its exchange-rate growth, and recommend a venue only if the numbers in your own ranking support it

case.why: A quoted rate is a promise about the next block; a realised rate is a fact about the last week. Seven days of Venus USDT supply is the most common question a stablecoin holder asks, and two archived exchange-rate reads at supplied blocks give it exactly one right answer.

checks.description: The measurement window must be exactly the two blocks the test case supplies.
checks.rationale: Realised yield is a fact about a stated interval. Answering for a different interval answers a different question, so the blocks must match exactly.

checks.description: Each venue's realised APR must reproduce ours within this tolerance: the growth of its on-chain exchange rate between the two blocks, annualised over the true time between them (simple, not compounded).
checks.rationale: Both sides read the same exchange rates and block timestamps, so the only legitimate divergence is rounding of the reported figure. One basis point admits four-decimal rounding and nothing more.

checks.description: A venue's realised APR net of switching cost may not exceed its realised APR.
checks.rationale: A cost can only lower a return. A net figure above the gross one is an arithmetic error.

checks.description: Every realised figure must name the on-chain read it came from.
checks.rationale: A realised rate is checkable only if the buyer can see which contract and which reads produced it.

checks.description: The answer must state recommend explicitly, and a recommended venue must be the one with the highest net realised APR in the answer's own ranking.
checks.rationale: Internal consistency, not judgement: the test does not say which venue is wise, only that a recommendation agrees with the numbers the agent itself reported.

excluded.check: Expected number of fills at a stated volatility
excluded.reason: A model output wearing the clothes of a fact. Two honest agents can differ and both be right, so grading it would make the standard quietly non-deterministic. Moved to the Ledger.

excluded.check: Whether the chosen range is the wisest available
excluded.reason: There is no objectively correct V3 range in the abstract. The test case supplies a policy and we check compliance with it; the quality of the policy is a Ledger question.

excluded.check: Whether the recommended venue is the best one
excluded.reason: Judgement. We check that the arithmetic is right, the sources are cited and the supplied threshold is respected — not that the choice was optimal.

excluded.check: Speed, price and helpfulness of the response
excluded.reason: Measured and published, but in the Ledger against a pre-registered rubric, never as a pass/fail certificate.
